# Communicating results
    
Week 9 tutorial goals:
  * Regression tables
  * Model predictions -- `plot_predictions()`
  * Save tables and figures

## Set-up
```{r,include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(modelsummary)
library(marginaleffects)
options(warn = -1) # suppress warning messages that do not disturb the program flow
```

### Make sure you have your project datasets and `W9.R` {-}
This week uses two files from your `Project` folder. They must be in these folders inside your R project folder:

+ V-Dem: `Project/VDem/vdem2000_2023.csv`
+ CES 2025: `Project/CES2025/2025 Canadian Election Study v1.dta`

### Load libraries {-}

#### Install new packages "modelsummary" and "marginaleffects" {-}
```{r,eval=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)

install.packages("modelsummary") # regression table
install.packages("pandoc") # to save regression table to Word doc output
library(modelsummary)

install.packages("marginaleffects") # model predictions
library(marginaleffects)
```


## VDem

```{r}
my_vars <- c("country_name", "country_id", "year", 
          "v2x_corr","e_gdppc")

vdem_selected <- read.csv("Project/VDem/vdem2000_2023.csv") |>
  select(all_of(my_vars)) |>
  filter(year==2009) 
```


### Scatter plot the bivariate relationship {-}
```{r}
ggplot(data=vdem_selected,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) +
  geom_point()
```

### Regression line {-}
```{r}
ggplot(data=vdem_selected,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) +
  geom_point(size=1,alpha=.5) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm",linewidth=.5) + # linear model, i.e. linear regression; linewidth sets the thickness of the line
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(seq(-5,100,by=10)))
```

#### Save ggplot as object {-}
```{r}
corruption_plot <- ggplot(data=vdem_selected,aes(x=v2x_corr,y=e_gdppc)) + # assign ggplot to corruption_plot
  geom_point(size=1,alpha=.5) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm",linewidth=.5) + # linear model, i.e. linear regression
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(seq(-5,100,by=10)))
```

#### Using `ggsave` {-}
```{r}
# specify arguments `filename`, `plot`, `width` and `height` of image file
ggsave(filename = "regressionLine.png",
       plot = corruption_plot,
       width=8, height=5)
```


### Regression table {-}

#### Table using `modelsummary` {-}
In Week 6, we used `model_parameters()` to read regression results. `modelsummary()` from the package `modelsummary` makes a regression table that is ready to put in a paper.
```{r}
corruption_model <- lm(e_gdppc ~ v2x_corr, data = vdem_selected)

modelsummary(corruption_model, stars=TRUE)
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Goodness-of-fit statistics {-}
```{r}
get_gof(corruption_model)
```

#### Select relevant statistics {-}

* Keep only "number of observations", "R-squared", and "adjusted R-squared" values
```{r}
modelsummary(corruption_model, 
             stars=TRUE, 
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared")) # select relevant goodness-of-fit statistics
```

#### Relabel {-}
```{r}
modelsummary(list("Base"=corruption_model), # list allows me to name the models
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("v2x_corr"="Corruption Index")) # rename coefficient
```


#### Save output {-}
Under Arguments > output, you can see a number of supported file formats: .docx, .html, .tex, .md, .txt, .csv, .xlsx, .png, .jpg
```{r}
?modelsummary
```


```{r,eval=F}
modelsummary(list("Base"=corruption_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("v2x_corr"="Corruption Index"),
             output="out.docx") 
```

### Clear environment {-}
```{r}
rm(list=ls())
```


## Canadian Election Study 2025

```{r}
my_vars <- c("cps25_age_in_years","cps25_news_cons","cps25_govt_confusing") #news consumption and internal political efficacy

ces_selected <- read_dta("Project/CES2025/2025 Canadian Election Study v1.dta") |>
  select(all_of(my_vars))
```

### Set "don't know" to `NA` {-}
Same as Week 7: use `if_else()` to make new variables, and keep them in the same data frame.
```{r}
ces_selected <- ces_selected |> # save the new variables in the same data frame
  mutate(govt_confusing=if_else(cps25_govt_confusing==5, # don't know or refused
                                NA, #if yes
                                cps25_govt_confusing), #if no
         news_cons=if_else(cps25_news_cons==7, # don't know or refused
                           NA, #if yes
                           cps25_news_cons)) #if no
```

### Check the new variables {-}
```{r}
table(ces_selected$govt_confusing)

table(ces_selected$news_cons)
```

`lm()` leaves out `NA`s automatically (Week 6), so we don't need to remove them first.


### Regression table {-}
```{r}
news_model <- lm(govt_confusing ~ news_cons, data = ces_selected) # model 1

modelsummary(list("Base"=news_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"),
             coef_rename=c("news_cons"="News Consumption"))
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Controls {-}
```{r}
news_age_model <- lm(govt_confusing ~ news_cons + cps25_age_in_years, data = ces_selected) # model 2

modelsummary(list("Base" = news_model,
                  "w/ Controls" = news_age_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("news_cons" = "News Consumption",
                           "cps25_age_in_years" = "Age"))
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

### Model predictions -- `plot_predictions()` {-}

`plot_predictions()` from the package `marginaleffects` shows the predicted value of the dependent variable at each value of the independent variable. The `condition` argument is the variable on the x-axis.
```{r}
plot_predictions(news_model, condition = "news_cons")
```

The same plot for the model with controls.
```{r}
plot_predictions(news_age_model, condition = "news_cons")
```

Now interpret: what does this mean?

#### Save output {-}
```{r,eval=F}
modelsummary(list("Base" = news_model,
                  "w/ Controls" = news_age_model),
             stars=TRUE,
             gof_map=c("nobs","r.squared","adj.r.squared"), 
             coef_rename=c("news_cons" = "News Consumption",
                           "cps25_age_in_years" = "Age"),
             output="ces.docx") 
```

### Clear environment {-}
```{r}
rm(list=ls())
```
